description: Seven proposed motion and editing recipes derived from named reference works. These are planning records, not executable templates or render.py options. The implemented registry remains templates.json.
timing_note: Every example beat below is a proposed adaptation. These times are not timecodes, measured cut boundaries, or transcripts from the reference films. These machine-readable example variants may differ from the alternate storyboards in REVERSE-ENGINEERING.md.
priority_note: Lower numbers mean earlier suggested implementation, based on usefulness to an agentic editor and asset/engineering requirements. Priority is not a prediction of audience reach.

recipes.name: Matchline
recipes.description: Join two different clips across a stable seam so bodies, objects, or trajectories appear to complete the same action. Each new pair carries the argument forward through a visual correspondence.
recipes.evidence_method: downloaded agency film and timestamped frame samples. Sampled states, not every cut boundary or sound cue.
recipes.reach_evidence: A roughly 7.6 million-view indexed snapshot was found during reference research. It is not a live verified count or evidence that the editing technique alone caused reach.
required_assets: At least two candidate pairs of owned or licensed clips with compatible poses, horizons, object shapes, or action trajectories.
Source in/out points and enough surrounding frames to adjust the synchronization.
A short message and the intended meaning of each pair.

inputs.name: clip_pairs
inputs.description: Left/right asset IDs, in/out points, correspondence landmarks, and the narrative relationship.

inputs.name: seam
inputs.description: Position, orientation, crop bounds, and the anchor that must remain continuous.

inputs.name: sync_events
inputs.description: Contact, landing, gesture, or direction-change times to align.

inputs.name: retime_limits
inputs.description: Explicitly permitted source-speed adjustments; dialogue remains at natural speed.

inputs.name: closing_copy
inputs.description: The idea that the paired actions should make clear.

example_beats.action: Introduce one clearly readable action and the central seam.
Reveal the second clip as the first action crosses the seam.
Replace the pair while preserving a pose, trajectory, or graphic anchor.
Use the strongest pair to resolve the stated relationship.
Hold a concise conclusion or brand mark.

prerequisites: Future implementation needs shot analysis, landmark tracking, crop planning, and frame-accurate media composition.
Confirm usable clip pairs before designing the final timing.
recipes.fallback: When the split cannot remain convincing, use a sequential match cut between the best aligned poses. Preserve the relationship without forcing a broken seam.
limitations: Success depends heavily on source selection and compatible camera geometry.
A shared silhouette is insufficient when actions or meanings contradict each other.
The current Pillow templates do not track subjects, retime footage, or construct these composites.
evaluation_checks: Measure landmark error and direction continuity around the seam at each join.
Check that crop changes do not remove the subject or hide the action being compared.
Review synchronization at normal speed and frame by frame around the contact event.
Confirm that each pair communicates the intended relationship without explanatory overload.

sound_direction.direction: Place an approved transient at the shared action contact; crossfade surrounding ambience. Preserve natural dialogue speed.
sound_direction.implemented_starter_support: One supplied audio track; no generated cue mix or animation-to-audio alignment.

recipes.name: Obsidian Product Journey
recipes.description: Follow one real product task through intention, interaction, result, and an artifact. Perspective, focus, and restrained camera movement preserve the same spatial context across the journey.
recipes.evidence_method: downloaded official film and timestamped frame samples. No production software or causal performance claim established.
recipes.reach_evidence: High-craft reference; no verified public audience metric was established.
required_assets: Approved screen captures, recordings, or reproducible UI states from one working product flow.
Actual output artifact and a view that shows where it belongs in the product.
Brand typography, palette, and closing mark.

inputs.name: ui_states
inputs.description: Ordered asset IDs, state names, focal rectangles, and the action responsible for each state change.

inputs.name: interaction_events
inputs.description: Cursor destinations, selections, typing events, and their resulting UI changes.

inputs.name: camera_poses
inputs.description: Bounded position, perspective, scale, and focus values for each beat.

inputs.name: reading_holds
inputs.description: Frames reserved for understanding the important text or result after motion settles.

inputs.name: brand
inputs.description: Product name, palette, font assets, and closing mark.

example_beats.action: Establish the product canvas and the task's starting state.
Frame one input or decision and show the corresponding interaction.
Reveal the actual result in the same spatial context.
Show the document, edit, report, or other useful output in readable detail.
Pull back to explain where the result fits in the workflow.
Clear the interface and hold the product identity.

prerequisites: Future implementation needs deterministic media/state playback and coordinated perspective, cursor, and focus animation.
Approve the source product flow and text before designing its camera choreography.
recipes.fallback: Use straight-on crops of the same approved UI states, with short movements between focal rectangles and generous reading holds.
limitations: It cannot demonstrate an absent product capability; every meaningful state must come from a supplied or approved source.
Blur and perspective must not conceal the feature being explained.
Prism's current image panels are not an implementation of this interactive product journey.
evaluation_checks: Verify that every interaction precedes and corresponds to its displayed result.
Compare each displayed state and artifact with its approved source.
Inspect focal text at the delivery size during the settled reading hold.
Check that the viewer can follow one task from input to useful output.

sound_direction.direction: Use a restrained bed, quiet interface event cues and a distinct arrival for the useful artifact. Duck under narration.
sound_direction.implemented_starter_support: One supplied audio track; no generated cue mix or animation-to-audio alignment.

recipes.name: Living System
recipes.description: Grow a small set of brand primitives into an expressive system. Grids, dots, type, processed footage, and tactile textures change together while retaining a recognizable visual identity.
recipes.evidence_method: timestamped frames from the actual studio hero asset and creator case study. Release year confirmed; exact original release day and sound timing not verified.
recipes.reach_evidence: High-craft reference; no verified public audience metric was established.
required_assets: A supplied brand mark, typeface, and a deliberately limited set of geometric primitives.
Owned or licensed photographs or clips chosen to supply the human or tactile material.
A brief defining the single idea that the evolving system should communicate.

inputs.name: primitive_system
inputs.description: Grid, dots, type, spacing, stroke, transparency, and palette rules.

inputs.name: source_media
inputs.description: Media assets and the regions that may be transformed through masks, sampling, or halftones.

inputs.name: transformations
inputs.description: Meaningful transitions between sparse, dense, tactile, and resolved states.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Stable seed for procedural variation that must remain reproducible.

inputs.name: closing_message
inputs.description: The idea or brand identity that the system resolves into.

example_beats.action: Establish one primitive and the motion rule that defines the system.
Let that rule form a larger grid or field without changing its identity.
Bring human or tactile source media through the established graphic language.
Use the same rules to reveal a new expressive configuration.
Resolve the field into a clear message or brand shape.

prerequisites: Future implementation needs procedural drawing, repeatable media masks, and shared style tokens across scenes.
Approve a representative sparse state, dense state, and media treatment before rendering the whole sequence.
recipes.fallback: Use flat SVG or Canvas primitives and preprocessed source images with controlled masks. Preserve the visual grammar without requiring a 3D or fluid simulation.
limitations: A changing particle background alone does not explain an idea or constitute this recipe.
Source-media processing must preserve the subject needed to understand the message.
The current runtime does not provide this multi-scene procedural system.
evaluation_checks: Confirm the same primitive rules remain recognizable in every scene.
Render the same frame out of order and compare it for deterministic output.
Check dense states for flicker, aliasing, and illegible small type at the delivery size.
Verify that each transformation has a communication purpose beyond decoration.

sound_direction.direction: Let texture density follow the visual density curve; clear space for the final readable message.
sound_direction.implemented_starter_support: One supplied audio track; no generated cue mix or animation-to-audio alignment.

recipes.name: Impossible Reveal
recipes.description: Present one apparently impossible action, hold its visual premise long enough to be understood, then reveal a practical or editorial explanation that reinterprets what the viewer just saw.
recipes.evidence_method: record entry and creator production explanation. Original TikTok playback unavailable; no observed frame timeline or audio analysis.
recipes.reach_evidence: Guinness reports approximately 2.2 billion TikTok views verified on March 15, 2022 for the video posted December 9, 2019. This is historical evidence, not a current counter or a promise of repeatable virality.
required_assets: A storyboard specifying both the apparent action and the honest reveal mechanism.
Planned source shots with compatible camera, lighting, movement, and occlusion; clean plates if the planned effect requires them.
The actual reveal shot or supplied elements needed to demonstrate the explanation.

inputs.name: premise
inputs.description: The single impossible action the viewer should perceive.

inputs.name: shot_plan
inputs.description: Capture requirements, actor/object marks, camera poses, and continuity anchors.

inputs.name: composite_plan
inputs.description: Explicit masks, occlusion windows, clean plates, or matched cuts needed by the chosen effect.

inputs.name: reveal
inputs.description: The shot or transformation that exposes the practical explanation.

inputs.name: payoff
inputs.description: The closing reaction or callback that rewards the reveal.

example_beats.action: Establish the ordinary environment and the action's continuity anchors.
Show the impossible action clearly without explaining it yet.
Expose the practical explanation through a motivated view or action.
Hold the resolved view and a short reaction or callback.

prerequisites: Future implementation needs a shot-planning step and an effect-specific compositing workflow.
Validate the intended illusion in a short test before completing production.
recipes.fallback: Use a deliberate occlusion or a clearly staged before/reveal cut. If the supplied material cannot support a convincing illusion, retain the reveal story and omit the seamless-effect claim.
limitations: This cannot be reliably applied as a filter to arbitrary footage.
Generated or mismatched source shots may break geometry, shadows, object identity, and camera continuity.
The current runtime has no tracking, rotoscoping, clean-plate, or live-action VFX implementation.
evaluation_checks: Check the action and explanation are understandable without a verbal tutorial.
Inspect mask edges, contact shadows, geometry, and object continuity around the reveal.
Confirm the reveal answers the visual question created by the opening.
Review the effect at normal speed before inspecting individual frames.

sound_direction.direction: Preserve believable scene ambience, then give the reveal a deliberate accent or pause.
sound_direction.implemented_starter_support: One supplied audio track; no generated cue mix or animation-to-audio alignment.

recipes.name: Approval Drama
recipes.description: Build a short workplace story around a recognizable problem, rising pressure, a concrete product intervention, a decision hold, and a visible payoff. Product footage earns its place by resolving the story.
recipes.evidence_method: downloaded studio film and timestamped frame samples. Timing belongs to studio-hosted version; other uploads can differ.
recipes.reach_evidence: IVERSON reports more than two million organic social views. This is a creator-reported campaign metric, not independently audited platform analytics. The award does not establish the cause of audience growth or company revenue.
required_assets: Supplied or licensed character footage with usable reactions and continuity.
Approved product captures that visibly solve the story's stated problem.
A script identifying the decision, its outcome, and a concise brand close.

inputs.name: story_problem
inputs.description: One familiar work problem the viewer can recognize immediately.

inputs.name: pressure_beats
inputs.description: Escalations that make the same problem more urgent without opening a second plot.

inputs.name: product_intervention
inputs.description: The real UI actions and resulting artifact that resolve the problem.

inputs.name: decision_and_reaction
inputs.description: The pending decision, suspense cue, actual answer in the story, and matching reaction clip.

inputs.name: brand_close
inputs.description: Final message, mark, and optional call to action.

example_beats.action: Establish the work problem and the person who needs it solved.
Escalate the same problem through one or two readable reactions.
Demonstrate the product making a useful change and show its output.
Hold for the consequential answer using a quiet visual cue.
Show the answer and the matching human response.
Let the brand inherit the resolution with a brief closing card.

prerequisites: Future implementation needs a narrative planner, shot-role metadata, dialogue/cut timing, and reaction matching.
Resolve the story and available footage before selecting motion treatments.
recipes.fallback: Tell the same problem/intervention/decision/payoff sequence with approved narration, product footage, and an explicitly fictional message graphic when compatible character footage is unavailable.
limitations: It is a story and editing structure, not a transition preset.
A staged message or reaction must not be presented as a real customer testimonial or measured result.
The current runtime does not assemble dialogue-driven live-action stories.
evaluation_checks: Verify that the opening problem, product action, and final answer refer to the same task.
Check that each reaction matches the answer and preserves character continuity.
Keep the decision hold readable without making it an arbitrary pause.
Confirm that the useful product output is visible before the brand close.

sound_direction.direction: Prioritize dialogue, reduce the music during the decision hold, and leave room for the human reaction.
sound_direction.implemented_starter_support: One supplied audio track; no generated cue mix or animation-to-audio alignment.

recipes.name: Material Language
recipes.description: Introduce two distinct visual grammars, discover a shared behavior, and transform them into one creative world. Persistent correspondences give the sequence a narrative instead of a sequence of unrelated effects.
recipes.evidence_method: creator production breakdown and public stage still. No original-film timeline or sound analysis; no claim about production software.
recipes.reach_evidence: High-craft reference with a confirmed Config 2026 presentation context; no verified audience metric was established.
required_assets: Two deliberately distinct sets of supplied shapes, typography, textures, or imagery.
Designed intermediate states that explain how elements correspond across the two grammars.
A final composition expressing the combined idea.

inputs.name: grammar_a
inputs.description: Initial rules for shape, material, color, motion, and density.

inputs.name: grammar_b
inputs.description: A contrasting but compatible second set of rules.

inputs.name: correspondences
inputs.description: Specific element-to-element or behavior-to-behavior relationships that justify each transformation.

inputs.name: shared_behavior
inputs.description: The motion or relationship through which the two systems discover a common language.

inputs.name: resolved_world
inputs.description: The final integrated composition and the idea it should communicate.

example_beats.action: Introduce the two grammars as distinct, readable systems.
Find one shared behavior or shape correspondence.
Let an identifiable element carry that relationship through a material change.
Show the range of ideas made possible by the combined language.
Settle into a coherent final world and a concise closing identity.

prerequisites: Future implementation needs art-directed state design, correspondence-aware transforms, and consistent style constraints across scenes.
Review the intermediate states before committing to simulation or complex 3D work.
recipes.fallback: Limit both grammars to a few 2D primitives and use designed masks, shape interpolation, and match cuts while preserving the conceptual relationship.
limitations: This needs more art direction than a generic template with replaceable text fields.
Unrelated generated clips with matching colors do not preserve a visual grammar.
The current runtime does not implement material simulation or correspondence-aware multi-scene transformation.
evaluation_checks: Identify the carried element or behavior at every transformation boundary.
Check that each grammar remains recognizable before the combined state appears.
Verify that the final world visibly explains the relationship introduced at the start.
Review transitions at normal speed for continuity and settled moments for comprehension.

sound_direction.direction: Assign distinct textures to the initial systems, then combine their motifs when the systems cooperate.
sound_direction.implemented_starter_support: One supplied audio track; no generated cue mix or animation-to-audio alignment.

recipes.name: Elastic Interface
recipes.description: Carry one recognizable outline or focal anchor through search, voice, photo, and video states. The interface changes its job while maintaining shape, location, and a readable rhythm.
recipes.evidence_method: downloaded silent square portfolio excerpt and timestamped frame samples. Excerpt offset inside the montage is unknown. The montage combines several projects.
recipes.reach_evidence: High-craft reference; no verified audience metric was established.
required_assets: Approved visual states for two to four interface modes, including their meaningful content.
Vector outlines or masks with explicit correspondences between consecutive states.
A consistent palette, typography system, and focal anchor.

inputs.name: mode_states
inputs.description: Mode role, source asset, content, focal rectangle, and required reading hold.

inputs.name: anchor
inputs.description: The semantic shape or point that remains recognizable across transformations.

inputs.name: shape_pairs
inputs.description: Compatible vector paths or masks for each approved state transition.

inputs.name: interaction_cues
inputs.description: Typing, recording, selection, or playback events that justify each state change.

inputs.name: transition_budget
inputs.description: Separate entrance, settled hold, and exit durations; preserve time to understand each mode.

example_beats.action: Establish the outline and its first clear function.
Perform a search interaction and hold its useful state.
Transform the same anchor into a voice interaction, then settle.
Use a meaningful shape correspondence to introduce the image state.
Expand the anchor into playback or another approved moving-media state.
Resolve the modes into a single clear product or brand composition.

prerequisites: Future implementation needs deterministic interface state playback, vector/mask transforms, and semantic anchor tracking.
Check path compatibility and content legibility before selecting a morph instead of a cut.
recipes.fallback: Use a match cut or a simple motivated mask between approved states when a morph would distort the interface. Retain the same anchor and reading holds.
limitations: Matching colors or rounded rectangles alone does not establish semantic continuity.
The preview excerpt does not provide evidence for the full film's soundtrack or complete structure.
The current runtime does not implement arbitrary SVG morphing or multi-mode UI playback.
evaluation_checks: Confirm that the same anchor remains identifiable before, during, and after each state change.
Verify that an interaction cue explains every change of interface mode.
Inspect each settled state for readable content at the intended output size.
Check intermediate geometry for self-intersections, text distortion, and unintended scale jumps.

sound_direction.direction: Support continuous shape movement with a restrained settling cue; leave reading holds acoustically calm.
sound_direction.implemented_starter_support: One supplied audio track; no generated cue mix or animation-to-audio alignment.
